op1: 1.  Declares inadmissible, unanimously, the complaint under Article 4 of Protocol No. 7 to the Convention concerning the applicant’s right not to be tried or punished twice in respect of the charges of murder of N.V. and Ne.V. which were dropped by the prosecutor on 25 January 1996;
op2: 2.  Holds, unanimously, that there has been no violation of Article 6 of the Convention;
op3: 3.  Holds, by sixteen votes to one, that Article 4 of Protocol No. 7 to the Convention is not applicable in respect of the charges of murder of S.B. and V.B. and the infliction of grievous bodily harm on Sl.B.
op4: In accordance with Article 45 § 2 of the Convention and Rule 74 § 2 of the Rules of Court, the following separate opinions are annexed to this judgment:
p15: 15.  On 25 January 1996 the Osijek Deputy Military Prosecutor dropped the charges under points 3, 4, 6, 7 and 9 of the indictment, as well as the charges of theft of others’ property. He charged the applicant with a new count of grievous bodily harm for having shot at a child, Sl.B., on 20 November 1991 at about 7 a.m. in Čepin. The former point 8 of the indictment thus became point 4.
p16: 16.  On 24 September 1996 the General Amnesty Act was enacted. It provided that a general amnesty was to be applied in respect of all criminal offences committed in connection with the war in Croatia between 17 August 1990 and 23 August 1996, save for those which amounted to the gravest breaches of humanitarian law or to war crimes, including the crime of genocide (see paragraph 27 below).
p17: 17.  On 24 June 1997 a panel of the Osijek County Court presided over by Judge M.K. decided to terminate the proceedings against the applicant under the General Amnesty Act. The relevant parts of that decision read as follows:
p18: 18.  On an unspecified date the State Attorney lodged a request for the protection of legality (*zahtjev za zaštitu zakonitosti*) with the Supreme Court, asking it to establish that there had been a violation of Article 3 § 2 of the General Amnesty Act.
